roleNote: An example of what you can build from kit components. Start from it, change it, or ignore it; layout is your choice. Follow `must` (kit look and accessibility); `defaults` are this example's suggestions, change any of them.
copyNote: Not exported from agentic-ds-kit. add copies the source into your app (components/patterns/settings-form/) with this contract beside it. You own the copy: replace the demo data, rearrange or drop sections, and keep the `must` lines.
intent: Settings form example: a PageHeader over grouped fields (FieldSets in one Card, legend left when wide), a sticky SaveBar that names unsaved changes, an error summary Alert, and an AlertDialog before changes are lost. The demo is company billing details.
must: Use kit components from agentic-ds-kit for anything the kit has; no local cousins (tables, dialogs, rows, rules, charts)
Semantic tokens only (agentic-ds-kit/tokens.css); no raw hex, no primitive --color-* ramps
At most one appearance="solid" mode="primary" Button per view
Do not restyle kit components; change them through their props, slots, and tokens
Wrap every labeled input in Field (label, hint, and error wiring)
Group related fields in a FieldSet with a legend; on a wide form use layout="side" so the legend sits in its own column
Save lives in a kit SaveBar after the form, sticky to the bottom of the scroller, with scroll-padding so a focused field is never under it
Save is the only solid primary on the page; the error summary Alert gives its action appearance "outline"
Mark each changed field with Field changed and put the old value in its hint ("Was USD."); the SaveBar lists the same fields
On Save with errors, show a danger Alert summary with one Button per field that moves focus to it, and focus the Alert; field errors keep their hint
Discard, and leaving with unsaved changes, ask first in a kit AlertDialog that names the changes; Keep editing is the cancel. Closing the tab can only use the browser's own beforeunload prompt

Render inside a main landmark (wrap the pattern, or your page content, in <main>); header and nav chrome, if any, use AppHeader / SideNav (or other header / nav landmarks) and nav stays reachable on small screens
defaults: Company, Billing address, and Currency and invoices groups in one Card md, split by Dividers; swap in your own groups
Controls are md 36 wide and lg 40 below --grid-breakpoint-sm, where the Card frame drops and paired fields stack
The demo opens with two unsaved edits so the SaveBar has something to say; open with the saved values in your app
